title: Typed Event Shape Mapper and Backpressure Circuit
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description: Introduce a 'shape mapper' component in the usage-event onramp that computes a schema confidence score, performs non-destructive type coercions, and routes ambiguous events into a slowpath for deferred reconciliation. Integrate a backpressure circuit that gracefully throttles low-confidence traffic and prioritizes high-confidence requests to protect downstream analytics and the Console UI.
background: We continue to see bursts of malformed/ambiguous usage events from SDK versions and third-party integrations. Current hard-reject behavior causes customer-visible gaps and noisy SRE alerts. Teams have asked for a middle path that preserves data fidelity while avoiding large error spikes in the console and ML pipelines.
goals: Reduce hard-rejects for recoverable event shapes by 80%
Prevent tail latency and queue buildup in downstream processors under burst load
Provide observability (confidence score histogram + loss reason) and per-tenant throttling controls
acceptance_criteria: Shape mapper emits confidence_score (0.0-1.0) and canonical_shape tags for every ingested event
Events with confidence >= 0.75 follow fastpath and are delivered with <= 150ms additional latency
Events with 0.4 <= confidence < 0.75 go to slowpath rewriter and are rate-limited under burst according to policy
Events with confidence < 0.4 are counted against tenant rejection quota and subject to soft-drop policy
Expose metrics: shape_mapper.confidence_histogram, shape_mapper.fastpath_success, backpressure.active_circuits, per_tenant_rejection_rate
technical_design: The shape mapper is a pluggable stage in the ingress mesh. It runs a lightweight type-fingerprint pass (field-level heuristics, length/format checks, enum recognition) against a flexible schema set pulled from the schema registry. Each rule emits match weight; a normalized confidence_score is computed. Rules include soft-coercion (string->int when numeric pattern matches, iso8601 parsing with fallback), canonical key mapping, and a reversible rewriter chain for slowpath corrections. Backpressure circuit is a tiered leaky-bucket with adaptive thresholds per tenant and a global emergency circuit that shifts traffic to a degraded delivery mode (sampling + archival to cold storage).
implementation_plan: 1) Implement shape mapper library in Go, unit tests for common malformed cases
2) Add fastpath/slowpath routing hooks in ingress-proxy and metric emission points
3) Build tenant-level policy store (config + defaults) and admin controls in Console
4) Implement backpressure circuit module with leaky-bucket and emergency circuit flag
5) End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout to 10% of traffic, monitor metrics
6) Gradual rollout to 100% with rollback guard rails
testing_plan: Synthetic fuzz corpus covering historical malformed events
Load tests simulating 5x burst with mixed confidence scores
Canary A/B comparing existing hard-reject behavior vs shape-mapper with retention of rejected samples
Contract tests ensuring downstream consumers accept canonical_shape metadata
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deploy to staging, validate observability and metric deltas
Canary: 10% tenant traffic with real-time dashboards and automated rollback on SLA regression
Expand to 50% after 72h stable, then 100% after one week if no regressions
Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window and follow-up tidy-up PRs
risks: Over-coercion leading to data corruption: mitigated by reversible rewrites + sample retention
Unanticipated latency on the ingress path: mitigated by fastpath short-circuit and circuit thresholds
Policy misconfiguration causing tenant impact: mitigated by conservative defaults and admin controls
monitoring_alerts: IF backpressure.active_circuits > 0 AND per_tenant_rejection_rate > 2% for 10m -> P1 alert
IF average ingress latency increases > 40ms post-deploy for 5m -> automatic rollback trigger
